answer: Operator Continuity Ledger. Each identity inherits a ledger that tracks shared infrastructure fingerprints (IP ranges, build hashes, funding paths) across all identities its operator controls. When a new identity links to an existing ledger above a linkage threshold, the whole cluster's task rewards decay like a marble rolling downhill. An attacker must rebuild fresh, unlinked infrastructure for every clone, a ripple of cost per identity. The orchard of clones yields less than one honest node, so mass registration loses money.
